entities.summary:
George of Liechtenstein (b. 1360, Mikulov) was a prominent entrepreneur and business leader of the Medieval period, active in Mikulov. He was a key figure associated with the Mikulov branch of the Habsburg dynasty and played a significant role in the region's economic development. George's involvement in the textile industry helped establish Mikulov as a major hub for wool production, contributing to the region's prosperity during this period. His entrepreneurial spirit and business acumen were shaped by feudalism, religious institutions, and cultural exchange, making him a notable figure in the history of Medieval Europe.

George of Liechtenstein was a member of the nobility and held various positions of power, including that of the Lord of Mikulov. He was also a patron of the arts and architecture, commissioning several notable buildings in Mikulov, including the Church of St. George. His legacy can be seen in the continued economic growth and cultural development of the region, which he helped shape through his entrepreneurial endeavors.

The exact date of George's death is not known, but it is believed to have occurred in 1419. His impact on the region's history is still felt today, with his name being mentioned alongside other notable figures from the Medieval period.

George of Liechtenstein's story serves as a reminder of the importance of entrepreneurship and business leadership in shaping the course of human history. His legacy is a testament to the power of individual initiative and the impact it can have on a community and its future.
